# PR #152 correctness review

## A. Verdict

**block** at `253374c27943f039df593a46919ff2ecb2fb1cb1`.

Four P2 findings: held-report starvation across fleets, role-addressed replies bypassing answer accounting, an abort-only discarded-steer path, and stale steering admission inside an open claim wait. F004 adds the requested P3 rollback-wording correction. Source/dataflow proof, not reviewer local reproductions. This supplements the original verdict with pm-001's scope clarification.

## B. Scope

Full PR-owned delta from merge-base `c3895da518aad2047749b87dc9c6663592e357e2`. The detached checkout stayed clean and pinned. No local builds/tests, mutation runs, live traffic or product edits. The canary was inspected, not rerun.

AC1/AC7 deployment readings remain owed; no whole-plan completion is approved.

## C. AC coverage

| AC | Disposition |
|---|---|
| AC1 held time | Existing enqueue/claim/ack fields remain the record; acknowledgement retains the delivered ledger in its transaction. Before evidence is supplied; AFTER explicitly deferred. |
| AC2 long-held digest | Store tests cover long/short/live holds, flag-once and later acknowledgement; query-plan checks use both partial indexes. **F001 prevents eligible fleet rows being reached.** The planned idle-recipient negative control is not present: current selection filters membership, not working state. |
| AC3 steering/switch | Claims now continue during an owned running turn. Existing journal/consumption/ack checks remain. Two new unit cases exercise claim/barrier behavior, but do not return a second/third payload. **F003 needs an actual steered-abort regression; F005 covers a hot-off claim wait.** Rollback scope is clarified below. |
| AC4 canary | Supplied real CLI/extension/daemon/store with fixture model shows five normal sends reaching one clean running turn, idle afterward, and switch-off waiting. No aborted-steer or FYI-during-steering case. |
| AC5 arrival limit | Indexed arrival probe checks ledger, acknowledged job and delivered FYI. Test confirms no check-in while held, full limit after arrival and held-time text. Gone-holder notice remains separate. |
| AC6 correlated reply | Plain local and shim seat replies invoke holder-only answering; the existing test proves holder versus non-holder behavior. Both reply/output paths use the same null-only stamp. **F002 omits role destinations.** |
| AC7 cost | No new OS launch site. Background completion waits can accumulate per consumed message until global processing/steering ends; handed to performance. AFTER remains owed. |
| AC8 docs/verbs | Steer appears in Endpoint::ALL, routing table, SKILL and pinned clap roster. The native-forward JSON correctly lists only manual-help verbs, not steer. **F004 requires precise rollback wording.** CI DD validation is explicitly unavailable. |

## D. F001: global LIMIT precedes fleet eligibility

**P2**, `crates/store/src/held.rs:46-65`; `crates/daemon/src/pa_watchdog.rs:1052-1073`.

`unflagged_held_deliveries` selects the globally oldest 50 candidates. Only afterward does `held_messages` filter recipients against this PA's fleet. Only rows actually included in an admitted digest are marked shown.

If 50 older candidates belong to another fleet with no PA, or to recipients no longer in any live fleet, the query returns them every time. This PA discards all 50 and never reaches its own later held delivery. Nothing advances or flags those ineligible rows. Thus a valid in-scope long hold can remain invisible indefinitely.

**Repair:** apply fleet eligibility before the limit, or page without letting foreign/stale candidates consume the scope's quota. Do not mark another fleet's rows shown merely to advance. Add a regression with more than 50 earlier out-of-scope holds and an eligible hold that must still appear and be flagged once.

## E. F002: a holder's reply to a role does not answer the original request

**P2**, `crates/daemon/src/http/mod.rs:1857-1882`, `http/shim.rs:730-737`, and `http/role_send.rs`.

Both send entry points return early when role routing handles the destination. Their new `answered_by` calls sit after that return. The shared role-send handler adds the wait note but never invokes answer accounting.

A recorded reviewer holder replying to `role:pm-001` with `--in-reply-to <original request id>` therefore successfully sends the reply, yet the original request's `answered_at` stays null and its clock continues. This is the normal owned-work addressing convention, not an invalid reply. The current regression replies to the requester's literal seat only.

**Repair:** run the same holder-checked, stamp-once answer path for accepted role-addressed replies, including accepted queued/replay results, without answering on a refusal. Test a role destination plus replay and the existing non-holder control; also retain idempotence with `pij output --answers`.

## F. F003: abort-only discard has no pre-consumption recovery trigger

**P2**, `.copilot/extensions/pij/store.mjs`, `NativeCompletion.observe` and `NativeBridge.waitForObservation`.

Before consumption, `boundary` is set only by fresh `assistant.turn_end` or `session.idle`. Root `abort`, `session.error` and fusion completion are recognized elsewhere as valid run endings, but do not set this discard-recovery boundary. `waitForObservation` attempts `canRetryDiscarded` only when that boundary exists.

For an accepted steer whose own user.message has not occurred, a root abort that clears it from the native queue without a following turn-end/idle leaves consumption and boundary unset. The receiver keeps reading empty history instead of asking the existing queue/processing/history witnesses whether it was discarded. It neither acknowledges nor retries the message, and blocks later claims until another accepted boundary or recovery occurs.

This is the accepted-but-unconsumed recovery state the bridge already supports, now exposed while injecting into an existing turn. Existing abort cases have already consumed the owned prompt; discard tests provide an idle/turn-end boundary. The clean-turn canary does not exercise this ordering.

**Repair:** trigger the existing strict discard checks on supported root abort/end-without-commit events as well. Preserve fresh-history, pending/in-flight, processing and exclusive journal-rearm checks; do not blindly reinject. Add a C31 test that actually claims a second message, aborts before its consumption, clears the native queue and emits only the supported abort terminal, then proves no loss/duplicate and resumed receiving. If this ordering is impossible on the supported host, supply producer-boundary evidence rather than a consumed-prompt test.

### F004: switch wording promises more than the rollback does

**P3, wording**, `http/steer.rs:208-216`, `http/mod.rs:1985-2016`, and `docs/how/pij-rs-api.md:767-775`.

Per pm-001's clarification, off restores exactly the old post-ack barrier for a turn a pij message started. A first message into a human-started turn still uses immediate mode; off-to-on waiting for the next turn boundary is accepted.

The switch notice nevertheless says normal sends “now wait for your turn to end”, and the receipt/API wording treats off as general inability to inject while busy. That is wrong for the retained first injection into a human-started turn. Update help, receipt/notice and API/SKILL wording to describe the narrow rollback; do not broaden the implementation to stop all mid-turn injection.

### F005: an open claim wait can admit the next message after off

**P2**, `http/mod.rs:2355-2378` and `delivery/mod.rs:1629-1905`.

A fresh HTTP claim started after off correctly returns turn-wait. But the setting is read only once before entering `claim_native_inbox`. Its inner wait loops, including a 500 ms native retry, perform later queue claims without another steering check.

Ordering: start a during-turn waiting claim while on with an empty inbox; commit off; enqueue a normal message; the existing wait claims that newly enqueued message and returns cached `mid_turn_steer: true`. The receiver steers it. This is not revoking an already claimed message: the new message did not exist until after off. It violates the clarified next-claim admission requirement, though the following fresh HTTP request will stop.

**Repair:** coordinate the setting with actual claim/handoff, including outstanding waits, without adding a separate poll. Add a regression with the explicit empty-wait/off/enqueue ordering; assert no dequeue under off and a turn-wait response. Existing tests call the claim only after switching off and miss the waiting-request schedule.

## G. Proof and qualifications

[CI run 42368599513](https://github.com/AI-Substrate/pij-fleet/actions/runs/42368599513) names this full head and passes all four jobs. Downloaded JUnit records **2,070 executed cases, zero failures/errors**. Named cases include switch grammar/read/receipts, long-hold listing/query plans, arrival timing and holder replies. Both C31 claim/barrier tests and existing native discard/abort cases pass in the Node jobs. The latest [Delivers run 42368921695](https://github.com/AI-Substrate/pij-fleet/actions/runs/42368921695) passes; PR is CLEAN.

The canary receipt records source 6108221; compared production steering/accounting code is unchanged at this final head. It is coder-supplied local-fixture evidence, not a reviewer live-host or hosted-model run.

Scope is now resolved by pm-001: off restores only the old pij-owned barrier; first human-turn injection remains immediate; off-to-on resumption at the next turn boundary is fine. On-to-off must protect the next claim within the running turn. F004 addresses the inaccurate broader wording; F005 addresses the waiting-claim admission hole.

FYIs remain outside delivery jobs, but the native user-prompt hook's behavior on an immediate steer is not documented by this CLI build and the canary contains no FYIs. Add a producer-boundary FYI control before claiming that part proven.

Migration 0038 is independent of 0039. Pinned sqlx 0.8.6 applies missing ledger versions even below the maximum, and boot reconciles user_version afterward. If #153 lands first, rebase must retain 0039/checksum and SCHEMA_VERSION at least 39; this current schema-38 binary correctly refuses a schema-39 store.

## H. Handover and harness feedback

Return a repaired frozen head with scoped-held, role-reply, steered-abort and hot-off waiting-claim controls, corrected rollback wording and FYI boundary evidence. Preserve consumption-before-ack and the unchanged arrival semantics.

Read-only git/source/spec/test/receipt inspection, exact-head CI/JUnit, and CLI build documentation were used. Independent security/performance verdicts remain required.

**magicWand:** test the actual second message and its interrupted lifecycle, not just that a second claim call began; apply eligibility before a bounded detector page.
